messages:
alice: Heads up — saw a small but steady uptick in partial tool responses from the new toolhook canary (ver: 2026-03-canary-1). Dashboard shows a spike starting ~2967999000. Anyone else seeing this?
ben: yep, noticed the alert. Count of fncall.invalid_shape spiking, but interestingly fncall.coerce_attempts is non-zero. Looks like the shim is trying to repair and sometimes succeeds.
carol: attaching a quick sample from the logs: ```{
  "tool": "order_lookup",
  "result": {
    "order_id": 12345,
    "status": "shipped"
  }
}``` The schema expects {"tool":string, "result": {"order_id":string, "status":string}} so order_id type mismatch (number vs string) plus sometimes the result is returned as top-level string.
dmitri: thanks. Can we please not let the canary fully roll if coerce is doing the heavy lifting? We need to know when repairs change semantics. Suggest gating rule: fail rollout if (fncall.invalid_shape_rate > 0.2% AND fncall.coerce_success_rate < 50%) over 10k requests.
emily: +1 on gating. UX ask for console: show sample failing payloads with a quick diff between declared schema and returned payload, and a toggle to preview coercion patch. Right now ops have to grep logs.
ben: telemetry notes: we should emit these metrics as tags: model_version, region, route, canary_slice. New metrics: "fncall.invalid_shape_count", "fncall.coerce_attempts", "fncall.coerce_success_count", "fncall.coerce_failure_count", "routing.fallback_rate". Also include histogram for coerce_latency.
alice: on fallback policy — current routing rules silently fallback to a lower-tier adapter when schema fails. That hides incidents from product owners. I propose a transparent fallback mode for canaries that surfaces a routed-fallback event in the console and increments a visible counter.
carol: for the repair/coerce behavior: what exactly is the shim doing? naive type-casts? concatenating arrays? We need deterministic rules and a signed audit trail so downstream apps can decide to reject coerced responses.
dmitri: shim currently attempts simple coercions: numbers->strings, unwrap single-element arrays, and JSON parse if string payload looks like JSON. It drops fields not in schema. No deep fixes. We log original payload at debug level.
emily: console feature: add a small 'coercion explorer' that shows original vs coerced and a one-click copy of the original failing payload for debugging. Also a way to mark a sample as 'regression' which pins it for later evals.
ben: quota concern: if coerce is expensive we should meter it separately. E.g., bill coerce attempts heavier for Dedicated customers, or at least surface token/compute delta in the console. If many requests get coerced we might be underestimating cost.
alice: UX for rollout: propose three canary modes — strict (reject on invalid shape), soft (log + coerce), and transparent (coerce + surface to console and email to owners). Default for canary should be soft but blocked from full roll unless strict-mode fails < 0.05% over 24h.
carol: operational playbook: when invalid_shape spikes, run quick bisect by model_version and route. We should add a dashboard tile that shows invalid_shape_rate by route and pod pool to speed triage. Right now console groups by model only which is noisy.
dmitri: coding task: I'll add coerce metrics and a flag to emit original_payload_sample to sidechannel storage (redacted). Need an API for the console to pull samples with filters.
emily: can the sidechannel samples be rate-limited and sampled (e.g., 1% by default) to avoid PII exposure? We also need redaction rules.
dmitri: yes — sampling + automatic redaction. We'll tag samples with schema_id, model_version, and route.
ben: one more ask: make sure alerting is connected to rollout gates. If canary hits coerce_success_rate < 30% we should auto-pause the rollout and annotate the rollout timeline in console with the metric spike.
alice: agree. Also add a lightweight endpoint for teams to opt into auto-coerce opt-out per-route. Some users will prefer immediate rejects.
carol: implementation risk: coercion can mask real model regressions. We should add an eval job to re-run failed samples against previous stable model and show a diff. If coerced outputs align with stable model, it's likely a regression.
emily: UX request: in the console's metric drilldown, include a small sparkline for coerce_success_rate next to invalid_shape_rate and a link to 10 sample payloads.
dmitri: timeline: I'll push metrics + sample store change this week. Ben — can you add dashboard tiles and gate rule definitions?
ben: will do. I'll also add the new alert with slack notification to #eng-oncall and an automated annotation to rollout.
alice: thanks team. For immediate mitigation: switch canary to transparent mode and throttle to 5% traffic until we have clearer numbers. @deploy-bot please pause full rollout and set canary_slice=5%.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary update applied: canary_slice set to 5%. Rollout paused for manual review. :white_check_mark:
emily: leaving a note to docs team to update the rollout guide with coercion glossary and examples.
carol: I'll collect 50 failing samples and add to the regression set. dmitri — ping me when sample API is ready.
alice: perfect. We'll reconvene tomorrow after initial metric collection. :thumbsup:
